text: Package Windows runtime redistributables (VC++ runtimes, .NET, WebView2, legacy DirectX) as per-prefix dependencies rather than runtime downloads.
Bound Windows background services, scheduled tasks and autostart entries inside a prefix by the owning component's lifecycle.
Support per-application personality version pinning (multiple Wine/Proton builds coexisting via package multi-versioning) surfaced in native UI.
Accept a Windows-personality scoping decision at V0 as the only V0 Windows deliverable.
Bring Wine up on the Linux personality and run the Wine test suite nightly in CI as non-gated V1 work; define the W1 corpus and per-title scenario harness.

Adopt a clean-room policy for the Windows personality mirroring Wine's rules: no disassembly of Microsoft binaries, exclusion of contributors exposed to leaked Windows source, and no bundling of Microsoft redistributables or fonts.
rationale: Any taint in the Win32 reimplementation exposes the whole project to copyright claims.

text: Define a policy that compatibility work never circumvents DRM or anti-tamper protections and document DMCA 1201 and EU equivalent exposure.
rationale: Gaming compatibility attracts circumvention pressure and a single incident can end the project legally.

text: Decide the approach to anti-cheat vendors (EAC, BattlEye) including required legal agreements and whether the project entity is able to sign them.
rationale: Meaningful Windows gaming compatibility depends on vendor cooperation that only a legal entity can obtain.

text: Define an upstream-contribution policy for Wine, Proton, DXVK and VKD3D: no long-lived Wine fork, upstream-first patches, and LGPL source provision for any modified Wine builds shipped.
rationale: Forking Wine is unsustainable and LGPL compliance for shipped builds is mandatory.

text: Does placing NT-object or PE-loading emulation in the GPLv2 kernel create license conflicts with LGPL Wine components, or must all Win32 emulation remain in userspace?
rationale: The answer constrains the Windows personality architecture before implementation starts.

lens: Build, toolchain, CI and test infrastructure
text: Integrate the Wine conformance test suite and a curated Windows application and game smoke corpus into nightly CI on GPU-equipped lab machines.
rationale: Windows gaming is a major product objective in §48 and regressions there are invisible to QEMU-only testing.

lens: Boot, firmware, platform security and identity
text: Run each Windows application in its own component with its own registry and prefix and the compatibility-default capability set, so one compromised game cannot read another application's files or credentials.
rationale: A single shared Wine prefix with user-wide authority would make the Windows personality the weakest point of the whole system.

lens: Boot, firmware, platform security and identity
text: Research whether measured boot and kernel lockdown can provide a platform-integrity signal that Windows anti-cheat vendors would accept in lieu of kernel drivers, and document the likely outcome for gaming compatibility claims.
rationale: §56.2 notes anti-cheat realities; lockdown makes anti-cheat kernel drivers impossible so gaming claims need an honest position.

text: Detect existing Steam libraries, Wine prefixes, Proton compatdata and Bottles/Lutris configurations on attached volumes and adopt them in the Windows personality without re-download.
rationale: Gaming is a stated major objective and a 500 GB re-download is a decisive adoption barrier.

text: Provide case-insensitive, case-preserving filesystem semantics for the Windows personality's view of user data without imposing them on native or Linux views.
rationale: Win32 applications break on case-sensitive storage and gaming compatibility depends on it.

text: Publicly document games and applications blocked by kernel-level anti-cheat, and treat anti-cheat bypass as an explicit nongoal.
rationale: Gamers evaluating the OS need an honest answer up front, and the project must not pursue evasion.

lens: Research spikes and decisions that must precede commitments
text: Decide whether 32-bit x86 Linux and Win32 binaries are supported in the personalities, given that a large share of Windows games are 32-bit.
rationale: Dropping 32-bit silently kills the gaming objective; keeping it costs kernel ABI surface and personality effort.

lens: Research spikes and decisions that must precede commitments
text: Decide whether the Windows personality runs Wine over the Linux personality (fast path to results) or Wine ported directly onto the native ABI, with overhead measured on a fixed game benchmark set.
rationale: Layering Wine on Linux compatibility doubles translation overhead but layering on native requires porting Wine's Unix assumptions.

lens: Research spikes and decisions that must precede commitments
text: Publish a research finding on anti-cheat feasibility that states which kernel-level anti-cheat systems cannot work under the capability model and are therefore out of 1.0 scope.
rationale: Setting expectations early prevents a gaming objective from silently expanding into kernel compromises.

lens: Research spikes and decisions that must precede commitments
text: Decide whether a KVM-backed virtual machine personality is an officially supported fallback for Linux or Windows software the personalities cannot run.
rationale: A VM fallback changes the compatibility promise and must integrate with the same launcher, clipboard and file chooser to avoid the 'obvious VM' failure.

text: Provide a Windows/Win32 compatibility personality that runs existing Windows software.
Do not build a Windows clone; Win32 exists only inside the Windows personality.
Windows personality must expose Win32 APIs to Windows applications.
Windows personality must expose NT object semantics to Windows applications.
Windows personality must expose Windows process semantics to Windows applications.
Windows personality must expose Windows handles to Windows applications.
Windows personality must expose DirectX to Windows applications.
Windows personality must expose Windows filesystem semantics to Windows applications.
Windows personality must expose registry semantics to Windows applications.
Windows applications execute through a Win32/NT Personality layer.
Use Wine/Proton as the starting point for the Windows personality rather than a clean-room Win32 implementation.
Implement the Windows personality data path: Windows executable -> Win32 APIs -> Windows Personality -> native kernel API.
Windows personality must provide a filesystem translation layer (FS) from Windows semantics onto native storage.
Windows personality must provide a GPU translation layer (DirectX to Vulkan via DXVK/VKD3D) onto native graphics abstractions.
Windows personality must map NT objects and handles (Objects) onto native objects and capabilities.
Support PE executable loading (EXE and DLL).
Support the Win32 API surface required by target applications and games.
Decide which NT semantics (object manager, async I/O, security descriptors, sections) are emulated and to what fidelity (ADR).
Support Windows filesystem behaviour: case-insensitivity, drive letters, share/lock semantics, path length rules.
Provide registry emulation with per-application state stored in mutable prefix storage.
Provide DirectX translation (D3D9/10/11 via DXVK, D3D12 via VKD3D-Proton).
Provide Windows process behaviour (CreateProcess, threads, handle inheritance, job objects).
Windows gaming compatibility is a major product objective; gaming proof-of-concept is required by V2 and meaningful compatibility by V3 (§62, §63).
Decide whether Wine runs as Linux-personality software or is ported to the native ABI as a first-class Windows personality (ADR).
Implement per-application Wine prefix management combining immutable Wine packages with mutable per-app prefix state.
Run each Windows application as a Component with capability-limited filesystem and device authority.
Provide a Proton-style per-game/per-app compatibility configuration database.
Provide game input (XInput/DirectInput), audio, HDR and VRR passthrough for Windows games via native objects (§56.2 cross-ref).
Resolve whether 32-bit x86 Windows applications (WoW64) are supported at 1.0 and what kernel support that requires.
Compatibility must feel native to the user.
Double-clicking a .exe must launch it as a normal application window with no intermediate UI.
Do not present compatibility software inside an obvious VM.
Do not present compatibility software on a separate desktop.
Do not require a compatibility wizard for ordinary Windows or Linux software.
Windows applications must integrate with native notifications.
Windows applications must integrate with the native clipboard.
Windows applications must integrate with native graphics (compositor surfaces, scaling, HDR/VRR).
Windows applications must use the native file chooser for open/save dialogs, receiving file capabilities.
Windows applications must receive native input (keyboard, mouse, gamepad) through the personality.
Resolve how Windows installers (setup.exe writing into a prefix) become 'installed applications' visible in the launcher and system history.
Windows gaming compatibility is a major product objective and must be staffed and tracked as such; do not underestimate its scope.
Integrate Wine/Proton as the core of the Windows personality (cross-ref §48).
Integrate DXVK for Direct3D 9/10/11 to Vulkan translation.
Integrate VKD3D-Proton for Direct3D 12 to Vulkan translation.
Study anti-cheat realities (Easy Anti-Cheat, BattlEye, kernel-mode anti-cheat) and produce a per-vendor compatibility and policy assessment.
Decide the policy for kernel-level anti-cheat drivers that are fundamentally incompatible with the capability security model (refuse, VM fallback, vendor engagement).
Gaming input support in the Windows personality: XInput, DirectInput, raw input, gamepads, force feedback.
Gaming audio support in the Windows personality: WASAPI/XAudio2 mapped to native low-latency audio objects.
HDR passthrough for Windows games from DXVK/VKD3D through the native compositor.
VRR support for Windows games via compositor frame scheduling.
GPU integration for the Windows personality: Vulkan device access, explicit synchronisation, present timing, fullscreen/direct scanout path.
Games running via the Windows personality (cross-ref §56.2).
Windows applications running via the Windows personality integrated into the native desktop.
Gaming proof-of-concept: a named set of Windows games running with measured frame times.
Meaningful Windows compatibility: a published list of working applications and games.
Windows personality path: Win32/NT implemented over native kernel primitives (cross-ref §48).
